author: Russell, J. A.
title: A circumplex model of affect
venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 39(6), 1161–1178
claim: Eight affect concepts placed round a circle at 45° intervals (pleasure 0°, excitement 45°, arousal 90°, distress 135°, displeasure 180°, depression 225°, sleepiness 270°, relaxation 315°); 28 emotion adjectives shown to fall in that circular order by four methods: Ross's (1938) circular-ordering technique, multidimensional scaling of perceived similarity, unidimensional scaling on hypothesised pleasure–displeasure and arousal dimensions, and a principal-components analysis of 343 subjects' self-reports of current affect.
verified: abstract text (angles, 28 adjectives, four methods, 343 Ss) and bibliographic details, via WebSearch result summaries; the 28-word list via a course figure caption (psu.pb.unizin.org, Chapter 5: Dimensional Models). The full text and the per-word angles of Figure 2 were not accessible from this sandbox, which is why the page positions the words with 2013 data instead.
found_via: WebSearch: 'Russell 1980 "A circumplex model of affect" 28 affect words angles direct circular scaling table'; 'Russell 1980 circumplex abstract "principal-components analysis" "343"'

author: Warriner, A. B., Kuperman, V., & Brysbaert, M.
title: Norms of valence, arousal, and dominance for 13,915 English lemmas
claim: Source of every word rating on the page: 13,915 lemmas rated on nine-point scales for valence (unhappy→happy), arousal, and dominance (weak/submissive→strong/dominant), extending ANEW. Data file Ratings_Warriner_et_al.csv (CC BY-NC-ND 3.0), columns V/A/D.Mean.Sum, V/A/D.SD.Sum, V/A/D.Rat.Sum. verified: title, authors, venue, DOI, 9-point scale and scale glosses via WebSearch summaries of the publisher record and the NoRaRe catalogue; data authenticity by matching the file's extremes to known values (vacation = highest valence, pedophile = lowest, insanity = highest arousal) and its SHA-256 recorded in data.js
